standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of an elementary etale neighbourhood making all fibres geometrically irreducible
standard_prerequisites.reference: More on Morphisms, Stacks tag 057J (more-morphisms-lemma-normal-morphism-irreducible), invoked at proof lines 1127-1132

core_obligations: Pick an elementary etale neighbourhood (S'', s'') -> (S', s') with S'' affine and an affine open Y'' of Y' x_{S'} S'' containing y'' = (y', s''), set Z'' = Z x_Y Y'' so that Z'' is affine and Z'' -> Z_{S''} is etale, and apply the etale lifting lemma to obtain an etale morphism of affines X'' -> X_{S'} with Z'' = X'' x_{X_{S'}} Z_{S'} and the resulting closed immersion i'' : Z'' -> X'' (proof lines 1065-1079).

Verify for every such choice the conditions of the definition of a one step devissage: i''_*G'' = F'' by construction, Y'' -> S'' smooth of relative dimension n = dim_x Supp(F_s), kappa(y'') = kappa(y) purely transcendental over kappa(s'') = kappa(s), pi'' finite with pi''^{-1}({y''}) = {z''}, and dim_{x''} Supp(F''_{s''}) = n by etale invariance of dimension at a point (proof lines 1081-1110).

Repair the only condition that can fail, geometric irreducibility of the fibres of Y'' -> S'': take the irreducible component T of Y'_{s'} through y', use that kappa(s) is algebraically closed in kappa(y) to conclude that T is geometrically connected and smoothness of T to conclude that it is geometrically irreducible, then invoke the normal-morphism lemma to find (S'', s'') -> (S', s') and an affine open Y'' of Y'_{S''} with all fibres geometrically irreducible and T = Y''_{s''} (proof lines 1112-1133).
proof_roadmap: Build the diagram from an arbitrary affine choice: take any elementary etale (S'', s'') -> (S', s') and any affine open Y'' in Y' x_{S'} S'' through y'', set Z'' = Z x_Y Y'', and lift the etale Z'' -> Z_{S''} to an etale X'' -> X_{S'} with Z'' = X'' x_{X_{S'}} Z_{S'} (proof lines 1066-1079).

Collect everything that already holds for that arbitrary choice: the closed immersion Z_{S''} -> X_{S''}, i''_*G'' = F'', the smoothness of Y'' -> S'' of relative dimension n, pure transcendence of kappa(y'')/kappa(s''), finiteness of pi'' with a single point over y'', and equality of the dimensions of the supports in the fibres (proof lines 1081-1110).
Identify the missing condition: geometric irreducibility of the fibres of Y'' -> S'' generally fails and is the only obstruction (proof lines 1112-1118).

Fix it geometrically: the component T of Y'_{s'} through y' is geometrically connected because kappa(s') = kappa(s) is algebraically closed in kappa(y') = kappa(y), hence geometrically irreducible as a smooth scheme, and the normal-morphism lemma then supplies the elementary etale (S'', s'') -> (S', s') and affine Y'' subset Y'_{S''} whose fibres are all geometrically irreducible with T = Y''_{s''}; shrinking keeps Y'' and S'' affine (proof lines 1119-1134).
difficulty_reason: The lemma must upgrade a one step devissage (Z, Y, i, pi, G, z, y) of F/X/S at x, after an arbitrary elementary etale neighbourhood (Y', y') -> (Y, y) -> (S, s), into a fresh one step devissage of the pullback F'' on a newly manufactured X'' together with an open Y'' of Y' x_{S'} S'' and Z'' = Z x_Y Y'' (statement lines 1049-1062). The proof manufactures X'' by applying the etale lifting lemma to the composite Z'' -> Z_{S''} -> X_{S''} so that Z'' = X'' x_{X_{S'}} Z_{S'} while keeping X'' affine, and then verifies every clause of the definition except one (proof lines 1065-1110). The clause that does not follow from the construction is geometric irreducibility of the fibres of Y'' -> S'', and the proof repairs exactly that: it takes the irreducible component T of Y'_{s'} through y', converts kappa(s) algebraically closed in kappa(y) into geometric connectedness of T and smoothness of T into geometric irreducibility, and only then invokes the normal-morphism lemma for the final elementary etale (S'', s'') -> (S', s'') with all fibres geometrically irreducible (proof lines 1112-1133). The same passage also has to preserve pi'' finite with pi''^{-1}({y''}) = {z''} and the dimension n of the support in the fibre, both checked through residue-field equalities and etale invariance of dimension at a point.
